rows.evidence: Q1: Material & method / Tentative layout - a field experiment in Shiyan, Hubei during the 2011 cucumber season with three drip treatments (reclaimed water, 50% reclaimed water, groundwater) in 4 m x 4 m plots, with soil NH4-N and NO3-N sampled at 2, 5 and 9 days after irrigation and NO3-N profiles to 200 cm at start and end of season (Figs 1-3).
rows.notes: The study measures only soil NH4-N and NO3-N in the 0-200 cm profile; it reports NO3-N increasing with depth (interpreted as a downward leaching tendency) and 31-45% increases per 50 cm layer by season end under T1, but it never measures groundwater or drainage below the root zone. The statement in the Conclusion that contaminants 'must' enter the groundwater system is an assertion supported by citations [39,40], not an own result. The study therefore supports only a precondition (soil nitrate accumulation and downward movement) of the claimed groundwater harm, so upstream = true. In addition, all three treatments use drip; the comparison is reclaimed water versus groundwater, so the result is evidence about reclaimed-water irrigation rather than about drip as a technology (technology_mismatch flagged). No replication, dispersion statistics, site/crop variation, scale above plot, stated requirements or explicit limitations are reported for this effect; the water-quality table gives ranges for irrigation water, not for the soil nitrate result.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Single-season, single-site, three-plot experiment with no replication, no statistics and no groundwater sampling; the paper is a short note published in a hydrogen energy journal with much of the reference list unrelated to the topic.
